items.description: Секция отзывов с иерархией: один крупный отзыв засечным шрифтом на две колонки, остальные мелкие. Стена одинаковых карточек читается как шум.

Составной блок: импортирует card-040 из @/components/vibeui/ — команда установки приносит их вместе с блоком. Блок владеет раскладкой и своим текстом, частям передаёт только пропсы, их палитры --vibeui-<name>-* не трогает.

Блок самодостаточен: один файл, без npm-зависимостей, собственная палитра в локальных переменных --vibeui-testimonials-001-*. Число колонок и размер главной цитаты считаются от собственной ширины блока через container-запросы. Разметка семантическая: каждый отзыв — <figure> с <blockquote> и <figcaption>. Аватар — инициалы на подложке акцента: фотографии в отзывах чаще всего стоковые и портят доверие сильнее, чем их отсутствие.

Сетка перестраивается от собственной ширины блока: одна колонка, две, три. Ноль зависимостей, один файл, своя палитра.

en.description: Two testimonial marquees running toward each other: hover pauses the motion, reduced-motion stops it. Self-contained: one file, no dependencies, the motion is pure CSS.

The block is self-contained: one file, no npm dependencies, its own palette in local variables --vibeui-testimonials-007-*. A server component; the motion is pure CSS. Each marquee track holds two copies of the row (the second is aria-hidden) and animates translateX(-50%): as the first copy leaves, the second takes its place, so the loop is seamless. items.description: Стена отзывов, оформленных как посты соцсети: аватар-инициалы, ник, текст и лайк-счётчик, masonry на CSS columns. Пост выглядит честнее полированной цитаты. Самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей.
items.docs:
Составной блок: импортирует card-031, heading-001 из @/components/vibeui/ — команда установки приносит их вместе с блоком. Блок владеет раскладкой и своим текстом, частям передаёт только пропсы, их палитры --vibeui-<name>-* не трогает.

Блок самодостаточен: один файл, без npm-зависимостей, собственная палитра в локальных переменных --vibeui-testimonials-009-*. Серверный компонент. Masonry собрана на column-count с break-inside:avoid: посты разной длины ложатся плотно без строки JS и без измерения высот. Каждый пост — article с шапкой (инициалы, имя, ник), текстом и подвалом с сердцем-SVG и счётчиком лайков; счётчик форматируется через Intl.NumberFormat. Число колонок считается от собственной ширины блока: одна, две, три.

items.name: Анна Ковалёва
items.text: Собрала лендинг курса за вечер. Выбрала блоки в каталоге, скинула агенту — он поставил всё сам. Утром поправила тексты и запустила рекламу.

items.name: Игорь Демидов
items.text: Компоненты приходят обычными файлами в проект. Ничего не ломается при обновлении, потому что обновлять нечего.

items.name: Пётр Ляхов
items.text: Впервые агент не изобрёл свою версию секции, а поставил ровно ту, что я выбрал. Инструкция для ИИ в комплекте решает.

items.name: Мария Соболева
items.text: Два дня — и страница кампании в проде вместе с текстами. Успели к дате запуска, чего не случалось три года.

items.name: Дмитрий Хан
items.text: Дизайнер у нас один, а проектов пять. Библиотека закрыла рутину и оставила ему время на то, ради чего его нанимали. Секции совпадают с превью один в один, спорить стало не о чем.

items.name: Ольга Титова
items.text: Взяли три блока — ноль новых зависимостей. Лучшая часть.

items.name: Павел Гусев
items.text: Переопределили переменные бренда за час, и секции легли в существующий сайт без конфликтов стилей.

items.name: Ирина Белова
items.text: Раньше спорили о вёрстке. Теперь спорим только о текстах — и это прогресс.

en.title: Social Post Wall
en.description: A wall of testimonials styled as social posts: initials avatar, handle, text and a like counter, masonry on CSS columns. A post reads as more honest than a polished quote. Self-contained: one file, no dependencies.
en.docs:
A composite block: imports card-031, heading-001 from @/components/vibeui/ — the install command brings them along with the block. The block owns the layout and its own text, passes the parts props only and leaves their --vibeui-<name>-* palettes alone.

The block is self-contained: one file, no npm dependencies, its own palette in local variables --vibeui-testimonials-009-*. A server component. The masonry is built on column-count with break-inside:avoid: posts of different lengths pack tightly without a line of JS and without measuring heights. Every post is an article with a header (initials, name, handle), the text and a footer with an SVG heart and a like counter formatted through Intl.NumberFormat. The column count follows the block's own width: one, two, three.

ai.summary: A wall of testimonials styled as social posts: an initials avatar, a name, an @handle, the post text and a like counter with a heart. Posts of different lengths pack into a masonry on CSS columns, and the component stays a server one. Zero dependencies, one file, its own palette.
preserve: the card-031, heading-001 imports from @/components/vibeui/ — do not inline their code into the block or swap in your own; the parts receive props only
the local --vibeui-testimonials-009-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-card, border-border and the like)
the masonry on column-count with break-inside:avoid — posts of different lengths pack tightly without JS; an even grid would force the texts to be cut to one height
the varying post lengths: identically trimmed paragraphs betray editing, and the wall lives on the unevenness
the post anatomy — avatar, name, handle, text, likes: these details are what makes a testimonial look like a post rather than a landing page card
initials instead of photographs: a stock face in a testimonial is noticed and costs trust
the aria-label on the like counter — to a screen reader a bare number without a caption means nothing
the <style> block inside the component — it holds the palette, the masonry and the post
light-dark() in the palette: the component has to follow the surrounding color-scheme rather than ship a dark theme of its own
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself
adapt: the items array — the name, handle, post text and like count
the accent through the accent prop — it colours the eyebrow, the initials and the heart
the like formatting locale in formatLikes if the site is not Russian
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
notes: CSS columns lays the posts top to bottom, then rightward: the first item of the array lands in the top left corner, and the reading order runs down each column.
A wall needs volume: six to nine posts. Three posts in three columns is not a wall, it is three lonely cards.
Likes are part of the trust: round numbers like 100 and 500 look invented.
The posts have to be real — ideally with links to the originals at hand.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the block has to stay a single file.

items.description: Одна цитата гигантской засечной типографикой с акцентными кавычками и автором внизу. Заявление: у нас есть отзыв, который стоит целой секции. Самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей.

en.title: Full-Screen Quote
en.description: A single quote in giant serif typography with accent quotation marks and the author below. A statement: we have a testimonial worth a whole section. Self-contained: one file, no dependencies.
en.docs:
A composite block: imports card-107 from @/components/vibeui/ — the install command brings them along with the block. The block owns the layout and its own text, passes the parts props only and leaves their --vibeui-<name>-* palettes alone.

The block is self-contained: one file, no npm dependencies, its own palette in local variables --vibeui-testimonials-010-*. A server component. The quote is set in the system serif at clamp(1.75rem…4.25rem) computed from the block's own width, with text-wrap:balance evening out the lines. The quotation marks are ::before and ::after pseudo-elements in the accent colour: the opening one is enlarged and hung into the left margin, the closing one stays in the line. The author is set off by a short accent dash drawn with a ::before on the figcaption.

ai.summary: One quote filling the section: giant serif typography, accent pseudo-element quotation marks, the author below behind a short accent dash. The size is computed from the block's own width; zero dependencies, one file, its own palette.

the local --vibeui-testimonials-010-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-card, border-border and the like)
the giant quote size: this is a statement block, and shrunk to a "normal" size it loses its reason to exist
the pseudo-element quotation marks in the accent colour — they mark the genre before the first word is read and never end up in copied text
the serif face of the quote: the contrast with the surrounding sans separates a human voice from the interface voice
text-wrap:balance — without it the last line of a giant setting dangles as a single word
the figure / blockquote / figcaption semantics — this is a quote with an author, not a heading
the opening mark hung into the left margin at wide sizes: hanging punctuation keeps the left edge of the text straight
light-dark() in the palette: the component has to follow the surrounding color-scheme rather than ship a dark theme of its own
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself

the accent through the accent prop — it colours the quotation marks and the author dash
the quote typeface through the --vibeui-testimonials-010-serif variable if the brand has a display face of its own
outer spacing through className: the section fills its parent's width
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
notes: Keep the quote to 20–25 words: at a giant size a long text becomes the wall this block was not designed for.

One such block per page: a second one cancels the effect of the first.
The testimonial has to be real and the author fine with this prominence: it is the loudest quote on the site.
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the block has to stay a single file.

items.title: Рейтинги площадок
items.description: Ряд карточек с оценками продукта на независимых площадках: звёзды, балл 4,8/5 и число отзывов. Оценка на чужой платформе убедительнее цитаты на своём сайте. Самодостаточен: один файл, без зависимостей.
items.docs:
Составной блок: импортирует card-032, heading-001 из @/components/vibeui/ — команда установки приносит их вместе с блоком. Блок владеет раскладкой и своим текстом, частям передаёт только пропсы, их палитры --vibeui-<name>-* не трогает.

Звёзды — два наложенных ряда SVG: серый снизу, акцентный сверху, обрезанный по ширине на score/5 — дробная оценка закрашивается честно, без округления до целых. en.title: Segmented Testimonials
en.description: Testimonials sorted by audience segment: startups, agencies, product teams. The tabs run on radio inputs without a line of JS. Self-contained: one file, no dependencies.
en.docs:
A composite block: imports card-043, heading-001 from @/components/vibeui/ — the install command brings them along with the block. The block owns the layout and its own text, passes the parts props only and leaves their --vibeui-<name>-* palettes alone.

The block is self-contained: one file, no npm dependencies, its own palette in local variables --vibeui-testimonials-012-*. A server component: the tabs are built on radio inputs inside labels and :has() selectors — switching segments works without JS, and the keyboard gets the radio group's arrow keys for free. The active tab is filled with the accent and near-black text; a panel is shown by the rule ":has(input[value=N]:checked) → panel N", with up to four segments supported. Each segment holds a grid of two figure quotes.

ai.summary: A testimonials section with CSS tabs by audience segment: startups, agencies, product teams. Switching runs on radio inputs and :has() with no client JS, and every segment holds two quotes. Zero dependencies, one file, its own palette.

the local --vibeui-testimonials-012-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-card, border-border and the like)
the radio inputs with :has() instead of useState: switching has to work without JS, otherwise the block stops being a server component
the split of testimonials into segments — a visitor looks for a quote "from someone like me", and one common pile takes that chance away
the input inside the label: the pairing works without ids, so the block creates no identifier conflicts
the visible focus ring via :has(input:focus-visible) — a keyboard user needs to see which tab they are on
the accent fill of the active tab with near-black text — only dark text holds contrast on accent
the figure / blockquote / figcaption semantics of the quotes — these are quotes with authors, not cards
light-dark() in the palette: the component has to follow the surrounding color-scheme rather than ship a dark theme of its own
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself

the accent through the accent prop — it colours the eyebrow, the active tab and the initials
the radio group name attribute if the block appears twice on a page
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
notes: The radio group name is fixed: two instances of the block on one page would join into one group — rename the inputs' name when repeating it.
Up to four segments are supported: the panel rules are written for values 0–3, extra segments are cut off.
The :has() selector needs a modern browser (Chrome 105+, Safari 15.4+, Firefox 121+); without it only the first segment stays visible.
Hidden panels exist in the DOM and are reachable by in-page search — that is normal for CSS tabs.
The testimonials have to be real, and the segments should match how you actually split your audience.

en.title: Before and After
en.description: A testimonial unfolded into a story of change: a "before" pain panel, an accented "after" result panel and a confirming quote below them. Self-contained: one file, no dependencies.
en.docs:
A composite block: imports card-044, heading-001 from @/components/vibeui/ — the install command brings them along with the block. The block owns the layout and its own text, passes the parts props only and leaves their --vibeui-<name>-* palettes alone.

The block is self-contained: one file, no npm dependencies, its own palette in local variables --vibeui-testimonials-013-*. A server component. Two article panels in a grid: "Before" is set in a muted colour with dash markers, "After" is lit with a warm accent tint via color-mix and check markers — the contrast is visible before reading, through styling alone, with no red or green. Below the panels sits a figure with the quote and the author, set off by a rule. At narrow widths the panels stack into a column: "Before" always reads first.

ai.summary: A comparison section: the "Before" pain panel in a muted colour, the "After" result panel with a warm accent highlight, and a client quote below confirming the change. The layout follows the block's own width. Zero dependencies, one file, its own palette.

the local --vibeui-testimonials-013-* palette — do not swap it for your theme tokens (bg-card, border-border and the like)
the asymmetry of the panels: "Before" muted, "After" lit with the accent — equal panels turn a story of change into a comparison table
the warm "After" tint via color-mix from the accent rather than green: green and red in this library are reserved for status semantics
the quote below the panels — without a human voice the comparison reads as a marketer's promise, not an experience
the Before → After order at narrow widths too: a story of change is told in that direction only
the dash markers on the pains and the checks on the results: different markers scan faster than different colours
the semantics: the panels are articles with their own headings, the quote is a figure with a blockquote and figcaption
light-dark() in the palette: the component has to follow the surrounding color-scheme rather than ship a dark theme of its own
the transparent background by default — the component sits on the page background instead of laying a panel under itself
adapt: beforePoints and afterPoints — the pain and result items; the panel headings beforeTitle and afterTitle
quote, name, role — the quote and the author's caption
the accent through the accent prop — it colours the "After" highlight, the checks and the quotation marks
background — the component background; empty means no background, taking the page colour
notes: The before and after items work in pairs: every pain gets its resolution, and an extra item on one side breaks the mirror.
Three or four items per panel is the ceiling: long lists turn the story into a checklist.
Write the "after" items as facts with numbers, not adjectives: "in one evening" convinces, "fast" does not.
The quote must belong to a real person from this story, not a "composite customer".
Do not lift the CSS variables into globals.css: the block has to stay a single file.
